Example from this song: 雲のよう (kumo no you) = 'like a cloud' — from 雲 (kumo, 'cloud') + のよう (no you, 'like')

More examples:
• 夢 (yume, 'dream') → 夢のような (yume no you na, 'dream-like')
• 子供 (kodomo, 'child') → 子供のように (kodomo no you ni, 'like a child')
• 花 (hana, 'flower') → 花のように美しい (hana no you ni utsukushii, 'beautiful like a flower')

Note: のよう + な = modifies a noun (夢のような話, 'a dream-like story'). のよう + に = modifies a verb (鳥のように飛ぶ, 'fly like a bird'). みたい (mitai) is the casual equivalent.

name: 〜のようで (no you de) — it seems like / is like

explanation.en:
How it works:
The pattern Noun + のようで (no you de) means "it seems like ~" or "it's like ~" and is used to describe something by comparison. The で (de) here is the て-form of だ (da), allowing you to connect this comparison to another clause. It is a softer, more descriptive version of のように (no you ni).

Example from this song:
The singer describes their experience by comparing it to familiar things — making abstract feelings concrete.

More examples:
• 夢のようで信じられない (yume no you de shinjirarenai) — "it's like a dream and I can't believe it"
• 映画のようで面白かった (eiga no you de omoshirokatta) — "it was like a movie and was interesting"
• 嵐のようで激しかった (arashi no you de hageshikatta) — "it was like a storm and was intense"

name: 〜のような (like / akin to)

explanation.en: Comparative structure: noun + のような = 'a [noun] like [the comparison thing] / one akin to.' Modifies the following noun. 名残のような温もり ('warmth akin to a lingering trace'). Compare with 〜のように (adverbial 'in the manner of'): のような modifies a noun, のように modifies a verb / clause. The pair handles all noun-similes in Japanese.
explanation.es: Estructura comparativa: sustantivo + のような = 'un [sustantivo] como [comparación] / parecido a'. Modifica al sustantivo siguiente. 名残のような温もり ('calidez parecida a un vestigio'). Compara con 〜のように (adverbial 'al modo de'): のような modifica sustantivo, のように modifica verbo / cláusula. El par cubre todas las comparaciones con sustantivo en japonés.
explanation.pt-BR: Estrutura comparativa: substantivo + のような = 'um [substantivo] tipo [comparação] / parecido com'. Modifica o substantivo seguinte. 名残のような温もり ('calor parecido com vestígio'). Compare com 〜のように (adverbial 'à maneira de'): のような modifica substantivo, のように modifica verbo / cláusula. O par trata todas as comparações com substantivo no japonês.

name: 〜の方が (no hou ga: the ... one is more)

explanation.en:
How it works: Use A の方が (no hou ga) + adjective to express that A has MORE of that quality. It's the comparison pattern — 'A is more [adj] (than B)'.

Example from this song: 嘘の方がずっと痛かった (uso no hou ga zutto itakatta) = 'the lie was far more painful' — from 嘘 (uso, 'lie') + の方が (no hou ga, 'is more') + ずっと (zutto, 'far more') + 痛かった (itakatta, 'was painful')

More examples:
• こっち (kocchi, 'this one') → こっちの方がいい (kocchi no hou ga ii, 'this one is better')
• 歩く (aruku, 'to walk') → 歩いた方がいい (aruita hou ga ii, 'it's better to walk')
• 夏 (natsu, 'summer') → 夏の方が好き (natsu no hou ga suki, 'I like summer more')

Note: For nouns: A の方が. For verbs (advice): た-form + 方がいい = 'you should'. ずっと (zutto, 'much more') intensifies the comparison. This song's line powerfully says lies hurt MORE than the truth.

name: 〜はしない (emphatic negation)

explanation.en: Verb stem + は + しない is a strong, often defiant negation: 'won't (do that), no way'. かないはしない 'no enemy can stand a chance'; 捨てはしない 'I won't throw it away'. Stronger than plain 〜ない.
explanation.es: Raíz del verbo + は + しない es negación enfática, a menudo desafiante. かないはしない 'ningún enemigo está a la altura'; 捨てはしない 'no lo voy a tirar'. Más fuerte que 〜ない.
explanation.pt-BR: Radical do verbo + は + しない é negação enfática, frequentemente desafiadora. かないはしない 'nenhum inimigo é páreo'; 捨てはしない 'não vou jogar fora'. Mais forte que 〜ない.

name: 〜はじめる (begin to)

explanation.en:
How it works: Take the verb masu-stem and add はじめる (hajimeru, 'to begin'). This creates a compound verb meaning 'to begin doing something'.

Example from this song: つかみはじめた (tsukami hajimeta) = 'began to grasp' — from つかむ (tsukamu, 'to grasp') → つかみ (tsukami, masu-stem) + はじめた (hajimeta, past of hajimeru)

More examples:
• 降る (furu, 'to fall') → 降りはじめる (furi hajimeru, 'begin to fall — rain starting')
• 読む (yomu, 'to read') → 読みはじめる (yomi hajimeru, 'begin to read')
• 分かる (wakaru, 'to understand') → 分かりはじめる (wakari hajimeru, 'begin to understand')

Note: Compare with 〜だす (dasu), which also means 'begin to' but implies a more sudden or unexpected start. はじめる is a gradual, intentional beginning.

name: 〜はずのない (hazu no nai - not supposed to)

explanation.en:
Expresses that something was not supposed to happen, that it goes against expectations. はず (hazu) means "supposed to" and のない (no nai) negates it.

How it works:
Verb dictionary form + はず (hazu) + の (no) + ない (nai). It modifies a noun: "a [noun] that was not supposed to [verb]."

Example from this song:
来るはずのない朝 (kuru hazu no nai asa, "A morning that was never supposed to come")

More examples:
- 失敗するはずのないテスト (shippai suru hazu no nai tesuto, "A test that was not supposed to be failed")
- ここにあるはずのない鍵 (koko ni aru hazu no nai kagi, "A key that shouldn’t be here")
- 泣くはずのない彼が泣いた (naku hazu no nai kare ga naita, "He cried, though he wasn’t supposed to")

name: 〜はずのない (hazu no nai) — should not have / impossible that

explanation.en:
How it works:
The pattern Verb た-form (ta-form) + はずのない (hazu no nai) means "should not have ~" or "it's impossible that ~." はず (hazu) expresses expectation, and のない (no nai) negates it — the expectation was that it could not happen, yet it did. This expresses surprise at something unexpected.

Example from this song:
交わしたはずのない (kawashita hazu no nai) — "shouldn't have exchanged"
The singer is surprised by a connection or promise that logically should not exist.

More examples:
• ここに置いたはずのない鍵 (koko ni oita hazu no nai kagi) — "a key that shouldn't have been placed here"
• 会ったはずのない人 (atta hazu no nai hito) — "a person I shouldn't have met"
• 知っているはずのない情報 (shitte iru hazu no nai jouhou) — "information they shouldn't know"

name: 〜ばいい (it's fine if you / just do X)

explanation.en: Conditional 〜ば + いい literally 'if X then it's good' = 'just do X / it'll be fine to do X'. Gentle permission or encouragement: 決めればいい ('it's fine to just decide'). Adding さ at the end softens it further into reassurance.
explanation.es: Condicional 〜ば + いい significa 'si X, entonces bien' = 'basta con hacer X / hazlo y ya'. Permiso/aliento suave: 決めればいい. Con さ al final suena aún más reconfortante.
explanation.pt-BR: Condicional 〜ば + いい significa 'se X, então tudo bem' = 'é só fazer X / pode fazer X'. Permissão ou incentivo suave: 決めればいい. Com さ no fim, vira tom mais reconfortante.

name: 〜ばっか / ばかり (just)

explanation.en:
How it works: Place ばかり (bakari) or its casual form ばっか (bakka) after a past tense verb to mean 'just did' or after a noun to mean 'only/nothing but'. It indicates exclusivity or recency.

Example from this song: 始まったばっか (hajimatta bakka) = 'just started' — from 始まった (hajimatta, 'started') + ばっか (bakka, 'just')

More examples:
• 食べる (taberu, 'to eat') → 食べたばかり (tabeta bakari, 'just ate')
• 文句 (monku, 'complaints') → 文句ばかり言う (monku bakari iu, 'do nothing but complain')
• 来た (kita, 'came') → 来たばっかり (kita bakkari, 'just arrived')

Note: た + ばかり = 'just did' (recency). ばかり with nouns = 'only/nothing but'. ばっか/ばっかり are casual contractions. 遊んでばかりいる (asonde bakari iru, 'do nothing but play').

name: 〜べき (beki: should)

explanation.en:
How it works: べき (beki) attaches to the dictionary form of a verb to express 'should' or 'ought to.' It indicates a moral obligation or something that is expected.

Example from this song: 愛されるべき (aisareru beki) = 'should be loved' — from 愛される (aisareru, 'to be loved', passive of 愛する) + べき (beki)

More examples:
• 行くべきだ (iku beki da, 'should go') — from 行く (iku, 'to go')
• 知るべきことだ (shiru beki koto da, 'something you should know') — from 知る (shiru, 'to know')
• やるべきことをやる (yaru beki koto o yaru, 'do what should be done') — from やる (yaru, 'to do')

Note: べき is stronger than ほうがいい (hou ga ii, 'it would be better'). The exception is する → するべき or すべき (both are correct). べき implies duty or moral correctness.

name: 〜ますように (may it be that... — wish form)

explanation.en: Verb + ますように expresses a wish: 雨が湿らせますように = 'may the rain dampen it'; 合格しますように ('may I pass'); 元気でいますように ('may you stay well'). Standard wording on tanabata strips and prayer plaques (絵馬).
explanation.es: Verbo + ますように expresa un deseo: 雨が湿らせますように, 合格しますように, 元気でいますように. Forma estándar en tiras del tanabata y ema (tablillas votivas).
explanation.pt-BR: Verbo + ますように exprime um desejo: 雨が湿らせますように, 合格しますように, 元気でいますように. Frase padrão em tiras do tanabata e ema (placas de oração).

name: 〜まみれ (covered in, smeared with)

explanation.en: Noun + まみれ means 'covered in / drenched in'. Like だらけ but specifically for sticky/wet things — blood, mud, sweat, oil. Aqua Timez extends it to abstract nouns: 挫折まみれ 'covered in setbacks'.
explanation.es: Sustantivo + まみれ significa 'cubierto de / empapado en'. Similar a だらけ, pero para cosas pegajosas/húmedas. 挫折まみれ 'cubierto de fracasos'.
explanation.pt-BR: Substantivo + まみれ significa 'coberto de / banhado em'. Parecido com だらけ mas mais para líquidos/grude. 挫折まみれ 'coberto de fracassos'.

name: 〜まるで...のように (marude... no you ni: just like)

explanation.en:
How it works: まるで (marude) means 'just like' and pairs with のように (no you ni) or みたいに (mitai ni) to create vivid similes. It emphasizes how closely something resembles something else.

Example from this song: まるで人生だから (marude jinsei dakara) = 'because it's just like life' — comparing the situation to life itself, from 人生 (jinsei, 'life')

More examples:
• まるで映画のように (marude eiga no you ni, 'just like a movie') — from 映画 (eiga, 'movie')
• まるで夢のようだ (marude yume no you da, 'it's just like a dream') — from 夢 (yume, 'dream')
• まるで別人のように変わった (marude betsujin no you ni kawatta, 'changed as if a different person')

Note: まるで adds emphasis to the comparison. Without まるで, のように still works but sounds less dramatic. みたいに is the casual equivalent of のように.

name: 〜みたいだ (it seems like; it's like)

explanation.en:
How it works: Add みたいだ (mitai da) after a noun, verb, or adjective to express resemblance or conjecture — 'it seems like X' or 'it's like X'. This is the casual equivalent of ようだ.

Example from this song: The song uses みたいだ to compare feelings and situations to something familiar, creating vivid imagery.

More examples:
• 夢 (yume, 'dream') → 夢みたいだ (yume mitai da, 'it's like a dream')
• 死んだ (shinda, 'died') → 死んだみたいだ (shinda mitai da, 'it seems like it died')
• 春 (haru, 'spring') → 春みたいだ (haru mitai da, 'it's like spring')

Note: Before a noun, use みたいな: 夢みたいな世界 (yume mitai na sekai, 'a world like a dream'). Before a verb, use みたいに: 鳥みたいに飛ぶ (tori mitai ni tobu, 'fly like a bird').

name: 〜も〜も (mo ... mo) — both ... and ...

explanation.en:
How it works:
The pattern X + も (mo) + Y + も (mo) means "both X and Y" or "X as well as Y." It emphasizes that multiple things share the same quality or are included equally. It can also be used with negatives to mean "neither X nor Y" when followed by a negative verb.

Example from this song:
The singer lists multiple things that are equally important or equally lost, using も...も to give them equal weight.

More examples:
• 日本語も英語も話せる (nihongo mo eigo mo hanaseru) — "can speak both Japanese and English"
• 時間もお金もない (jikan mo okane mo nai) — "have neither time nor money"
• 父も母も元気です (chichi mo haha mo genki desu) — "both my father and mother are well"

name: 〜ゆく (yuku - literary 〜ていく)

explanation.en:
A literary/poetic form of 〜ていく (te iku), expressing a gradual change moving away from the speaker. Common in poetry and song lyrics.

How it works:
Attach ゆく (yuku) to the masu-stem of a verb. It replaces the more casual ていく (te iku).

Example from this song:
奪われゆく生命 (ubarare yuku seimei, "Lives being gradually taken away")

More examples:
- 消えゆく光 (kie yuku hikari, "Light fading away")
- 過ぎゆく時 (sugi yuku toki, "Time passing by")
- 変わりゆく世界 (kawari yuku sekai, "A world that is changing")

name: 〜ようで (you de) — as if / it seems like

explanation.en:
How it works:
The pattern Verb plain form + ようで (you de) means "as if ~" or "it seems like ~ and..." The で (de) is the て-form of だ (da), allowing this simile to connect to another clause. It describes the appearance or impression of something while continuing the sentence.

Example from this song:
しみ込むようで (shimi komu you de) — "as if soaking in"
The feeling is described as seeping deeply into the singer's heart.

More examples:
• 夢のようで信じられない (yume no you de shinjirarenai) — "it's like a dream and I can't believe it"
• 終わりのないようで疲れた (owari no nai you de tsukareta) — "it seemed endless and I got tired"
• 時間が止まったようで静かだった (jikan ga tomatta you de shizuka datta) — "it was as if time stopped and it was quiet"

name: 〜ようとして (you to shite) — trying to

explanation.en:
How it works:
The pattern Verb volitional form + とする (to suru) means "to try to ~" or "to be about to ~." The て-form version, ようとして (you to shite), connects this attempt to what happens next. It captures the moment of effort or intention, often when the attempt is difficult or interrupted.

Example from this song:
見つけ出そうとして (mitsuke dasou to shite) — "trying to find"
The singer is making an effort to discover something.

More examples:
• 逃げようとしたが、捕まった (nigeyou to shita ga, tsukamatta) — "tried to escape but was caught"
• ドアを開けようとしている (doa o akeyou to shite iru) — "is trying to open the door"
• 立ち上がろうとして転んだ (tachiagaro to shite koronda) — "tried to stand up and fell"

name: 〜ような (you na - like/as if)

explanation.en:
Creates a comparison: "like" or "as if." It connects a descriptive phrase to a noun, saying one thing resembles another.

How it works:
Place ような (you na) after a noun + の (no), or after a verb in dictionary form.

Example from this song:
ガラス細工のような思い出の破片 (garasu saiku no you na omoide no hahen, "Fragments of memories like glasswork")

More examples:
- 夢のような話 (yume no you na hanashi, "A story like a dream")
- 子供のように笑う (kodomo no you ni warau, "Laugh like a child")
- 嵐のような日々 (arashi no you na hibi, "Days like a storm")

name: 〜ような / 〜ように (you na / you ni: like / as if)

explanation.en:
Draws a comparison — 'like / resembling / in the manner of'. ような modifies a noun; ように modifies a verb or clause.

From this song: 夜明けを呼び覚ますような燃えるキモチ = 'a burning feeling like one that calls the dawn'.

More examples:
• 夢のような日 (a dream-like day)
• 泣いているように見える (looks as if crying)
• 鳥が飛ぶように (like a bird flies)

name: 〜ようにする (yō ni suru — as if doing)

explanation.en:
How it works: Add ように (yō ni) after a verb in dictionary form to express manner — 'as if doing X' or 'in such a way that X'. It can describe how an action is performed.

Example from this song: 言い聞かせるように (iikikaseru yō ni) = 'as if telling oneself' — from 言い聞かせる (iikikaseru, 'to tell oneself') + ように (yō ni, 'as if')

More examples:
• 歌う (utau, 'to sing') → 歌うように (utau yō ni, 'as if singing')
• 飛ぶ (tobu, 'to fly') → 飛ぶように (tobu yō ni, 'as if flying')
• 祈る (inoru, 'to pray') → 祈るように (inoru yō ni, 'as if praying')

Note: ように has multiple uses. With する it means 'try to / make sure to': 忘れないようにする (wasurenai yō ni suru, 'make sure not to forget'). Without する, it describes manner.

name: 〜を超えて (to surpass; beyond)

explanation.en:
How it works: を超えて (o koete) means 'going beyond' or 'surpassing.' 超える (koeru) means 'to exceed,' and in te-form it connects to the next action or description.

Example from this song: 限界を超えて (genkai o koete) = 'surpassing the limits' — from 限界 (genkai, 'limit') + を (o) + 超えて (koete, 'exceeding')

More examples:
• 国境を超えて (kokkyou o koete, 'crossing borders') — from 国境 (kokkyou, 'national border')
• 想像を超えた (souzou o koeta, 'exceeded imagination') — from 想像 (souzou, 'imagination')
• 時を超えて (toki o koete, 'transcending time') — from 時 (toki, 'time')

Note: 超える (koeru) is a versatile verb. を超えて in te-form often connects to what happens after surpassing: 限界を超えて飛び出そう (genkai o koete tobidasou, 'let's break past our limits and leap out').

name: 〜を追い越す (o oikosu - to overtake)

explanation.en:
A compound verb meaning "to overtake" or "to pass by." Combines 追い (oi, "chase") + 越す (kosu, "cross over").

How it works:
Use を (o) to mark the object being overtaken, then 追い越す (oikosu).

Example from this song:
風を追い越して (kaze o oikoshite, "Overtaking the wind")

More examples:
- 車を追い越す (kuruma o oikosu, "to overtake a car")
- 時代を追い越す (jidai o oikosu, "to surpass the era")
- 先輩を追い越した (senpai o oikoshita, "surpassed my senior")

name: 〜んじゃないの (n ja nai no) — isn't it that / could it be

explanation.en:
How it works:
The pattern Verb/Adjective plain form + んじゃないの (n ja nai no) is a casual way to suggest or gently accuse — "isn't it that ~?" or "could it be ~?" It wraps a statement into a soft question or challenge. It can be confrontational or genuinely questioning, depending on tone.

Example from this song:
怖いんじゃないの (kowai n ja nai no) — "aren't you actually scared?"
The singer challenges someone, suggesting they are hiding their fear.

More examples:
• 本当は知ってるんじゃないの (hontou wa shitteru n ja nai no) — "don't you actually know?"
• 好きなんじゃないの (suki nan ja nai no) — "isn't it that you like them?"
• 嫌なんじゃないの (iya nan ja nai no) — "don't you actually dislike it?"

name: 〜んでしょ (right?)

explanation.en:
How it works: Combine the explanatory ん (n) with でしょ (desho, seeking confirmation). This creates a casual way to seek agreement — 'right?' or 'isn't it?'. It's the casual form of のでしょう (no deshou).

Example from this song: 忘れてないんでしょ (wasuretenainddesho) = 'you haven't forgotten, right?' — from 忘れてない (wasuretenai, 'haven't forgotten') + んでしょ (ndesho, 'right?')

More examples:
• 知っている (shitteiru, 'know') → 知ってるんでしょ (shitterundesho, 'you know, right?')
• 好き (suki, 'like') → 好きなんでしょ (suki nandesho, 'you like it, right?')
• 行きたい (ikitai, 'want to go') → 行きたいんでしょ (ikitaindesho, 'you want to go, right?')

Note: んでしょ is softer than でしょ alone and adds emotional depth. It's very common in anime dialogue when a character confronts another about their true feelings.

name: 〜んな (nna - casual prohibition)

explanation.en:
A very casual contraction of するな (suru na, "don’t do"). It sounds rough and masculine, commonly used among friends.

How it works:
Contract the verb + な (na, prohibition) into a shorter form. 悩ませんな (nayamasen na) becomes a rough "don’t worry about it."

Example from this song:
頭悩ませんな (atama nayamase nna, "Don’t rack your brain")

More examples:
- ふざけんな (fuzaken na, "Don’t mess around!")
- 気にすんな (ki ni sun na, "Don’t worry about it")
- 泣くんじゃねぇ (nakun ja nee, "Don’t cry" - even rougher variant)

name: 〜ワケにはいかない (wake ni wa ikanai - cannot do)

explanation.en:
Expresses that something "cannot be done" due to social, moral, or situational reasons. It is stronger than できない (dekinai, "cannot") because it implies the speaker feels a moral or social obligation not to do something.

How it works:
Attach ワケにはいかない (wake ni wa ikanai) after the dictionary form of a verb. The verb describes the action that is unacceptable.

Example from this song:
誰にも邪魔させるワケにはいかないから (dare ni mo jama saseru wake ni wa ikanai kara, "Because I cannot allow anyone to get in the way")

More examples:
- ここで諦めるワケにはいかない (koko de akirameru wake ni wa ikanai, "I cannot give up here")
- 嘘をつくワケにはいかない (uso o tsuku wake ni wa ikanai, "I cannot tell a lie")
- 友達を裏切るワケにはいかない (tomodachi o uragiru wake ni wa ikanai, "I cannot betray my friend")

name: 〜今すぐ (ima sugu - right now)

explanation.en:
Means "right now" or "immediately." Combines 今 (ima, "now") + すぐ (sugu, "immediately") for urgency.

How it works:
Place 今すぐ (ima sugu) before the verb to emphasize immediacy.

Example from this song:
今すぐ伝えたい (ima sugu tsutaetai, "I want to convey right now")

More examples:
- 今すぐ行きたい (ima sugu ikitai, "I want to go right now")
- 今すぐ電話して (ima sugu denwa shite, "Call right now")
- 今すぐ会いたい (ima sugu aitai, "I want to see you right now")

name: 〜出す (begin to)

explanation.en:
How it works: Take the verb masu-stem and add 出す (dasu, 'to put out'). As an auxiliary, it means 'to suddenly begin doing'. It emphasizes the abruptness of the start.

Example from this song: 動き出す (ugoki dasu) = 'begin to move' — from 動く (ugoku, 'to move') → 動き (ugoki, masu-stem) + 出す (dasu)

More examples:
• 走る (hashiru, 'to run') → 走り出す (hashiri dasu, 'suddenly start running')
• 降る (furu, 'to fall — rain') → 降り出す (furi dasu, 'suddenly start raining')
• 泣く (naku, 'to cry') → 泣き出す (naki dasu, 'burst into tears')

Note: Compare with はじめる (hajimeru, 'begin to') which is a gradual, expected start. 出す implies suddenness and often surprise. 急に笑い出した (kyuu ni warai dashita, 'suddenly burst out laughing').

name: 〜出す (dasu - to begin)

explanation.en:
An auxiliary verb indicating the sudden start of an action. When attached to a verb stem, it means "to start [doing something]" or "to burst into [doing something]."

How it works:
Take the masu-stem of a verb and add 出す (dasu).

Example from this song:
二人歩き出す (futari arukidasu, "The two of us start walking")

More examples:
- 雨が降り出した (ame ga furidashita, "It started to rain")
- 急に笑い出した (kyuu ni waraidashita, "Suddenly burst out laughing")
- 走り出す (hashiridasu, "to start running")

name: 〜出す (to start doing; to burst out)

explanation.en:
How it works: Attach 出す (dasu, 'to put out') to the verb stem (masu-stem) to express a sudden or explosive beginning of an action — 'burst out doing' or 'start to do'.

Example from this song: 抜け出す (nukedasu) = 'to break out / escape' — from 抜ける (nukeru, 'to slip through') → 抜け (nuke, stem) + 出す (dasu, 'to burst out'). Also: 逃げ出す (nigedasu) = 'to run away' — from 逃げる (nigeru, 'to flee') → 逃げ (nige, stem) + 出す (dasu)

More examples:
• 走る (hashiru, 'to run') → 走り出す (hashiridasu, 'to start running suddenly')
• 泣く (naku, 'to cry') → 泣き出す (nakidasu, 'to burst into tears')
• 笑う (warau, 'to laugh') → 笑い出す (waraidasu, 'to burst out laughing')

Note: 〜出す emphasizes the sudden, often unstoppable nature of the action starting. Compare with 〜始める (hajimeru), which is a neutral 'begin to'.

name: 〜前に (mae ni - before)

explanation.en:
Japanese equivalent of "before" as in "before you idealize." It marks a point in time before an action.

How it works:
Place 前に (mae ni) after the dictionary form of a verb.

Example from this song:
"Cultivate your hunger before you idealize" → 理想化する前に (risou-ka suru mae ni, "before you idealize")

More examples:
- 寝る前に歯を磨く (neru mae ni ha o migaku, "Brush your teeth before sleeping")
- 出かける前に確認する (dekakeru mae ni kakunin suru, "Check before going out")
- 食べる前に手を洗う (taberu mae ni te o arau, "Wash hands before eating")

name: 〜故に (yue ni - because of)

explanation.en:
A literary and formal way to say "because of" or "due to." It sounds much more elegant than the everyday から (kara) or ので (node). You will mostly find it in written Japanese, poetry, and song lyrics.

How it works:
Attach 故に (yue ni) after a verb in past tense, a noun, or a na-adjective + な. It marks the reason or cause for what follows.

Example from this song:
愛した故に芽生えた悪の花 (aishita yue ni mebaeta aku no hana, "Because I loved, a flower of evil bloomed")

More examples:
- 若さ故に (wakasa yue ni, "because of youth")
- 知らなかった故に (shiranakatta yue ni, "because I did not know")
- 彼女が好きだった故に (kanojo ga suki datta yue ni, "because I liked her")

name: 〜次第 (depends on; up to)

explanation.en:
How it works: 次第 (shidai) after a noun means 'depends on' or 'up to.' It indicates that the outcome is determined by the stated factor.

Example from this song: 自分次第 (jibun shidai) = 'up to myself / depends on me' — from 自分 (jibun, 'oneself') + 次第 (shidai)

More examples:
• 天気次第 (tenki shidai, 'depends on the weather') — from 天気 (tenki, 'weather')
• やり方次第 (yarikata shidai, 'depends on how you do it') — from やり方 (yarikata, 'method')
• 気持ち次第 (kimochi shidai, 'depends on your feelings') — from 気持ち (kimochi, 'feelings')

Note: Noun + 次第 is a very empowering expression. 自分次第 means 'it's all up to me' — a common motivational phrase. 次第 can also mean 'as soon as' with verb stems: 届き次第 (todoki shidai, 'as soon as it arrives').

name: 〜気がする (ki ga suru: have a feeling that)

explanation.en:
How it works: Use [clause] + 気がする (ki ga suru, literally 'a feeling does') to express a vague intuition or feeling — 'I have a feeling that X' or 'it feels like X'.

Example from this song: そんな気がする (sonna ki ga suru) = 'I have that kind of feeling' — from そんな (sonna, 'that kind of') + 気がする (ki ga suru, 'have a feeling')

More examples:
• 会ったことがある (atta koto ga aru, 'have met') → 会ったことがある気がする (atta koto ga aru ki ga suru, 'I feel like I've met you before')
• 忘れている (wasurete iru, 'am forgetting') → 何か忘れている気がする (nanika wasurete iru ki ga suru, 'I have a feeling I'm forgetting something')
• うまくいく (umaku iku, 'go well') → うまくいく気がする (umaku iku ki ga suru, 'I have a feeling it'll work out')

Note: 気がする is for uncertain, gut feelings — lighter than 思う (omou, 'to think'). It's perfect for intuitive or emotional moments, which is why it fits so well in this song's reflective farewell.

name: せっかく〜のに/から (sekkaku: since the effort was made)

explanation.en:
How it works: Place せっかく (sekkaku) before a clause to emphasize that something special or effortful happened, and you should take advantage of it. Pairs with から (kara, 'so') or のに (noni, 'despite').

Example from this song: せっかく晴れたから (sekkaku hareta kara) = 'since it finally cleared up (don't waste it)' — from せっかく (sekkaku, 'with great effort/finally') + 晴れた (hareta, 'cleared up') + から (kara, 'so')

More examples:
• 来る (kuru, 'to come') → せっかく来たのに (sekkaku kita noni, 'you came all this way, and yet...')
• 作る (tsukuru, 'to make') → せっかく作ったから (sekkaku tsukutta kara, 'since I went to the trouble of making it')
• 休み (yasumi, 'holiday') → せっかくの休みだから (sekkaku no yasumi da kara, 'since it's a precious day off')

Note: せっかく + から = positive outcome ('since the effort was made, let's enjoy it'). せっかく + のに = wasted effort ('despite the effort, it was wasted'). With nouns: せっかくの + noun.

name: どうか (please / somehow)

explanation.en: Adverbial expression with two main senses: (1) 'please' (in pleading / praying) — どうか叶えて ('please make it come true'); (2) 'somehow' (in uncertainty) — どうか分からない ('somehow I don't know'). The pleading sense is most common, especially with imperatives or volitionals. More heartfelt than ください ('please give'). Smile for you's 心よ どうか遠く空を駆けて ('heart, please race across the sky') is a prayer to the speaker's own heart.
explanation.es: Expresión adverbial con dos sentidos: (1) 'por favor' (suplicando / rezando) — どうか叶えて ('por favor haz que se cumpla'); (2) 'de alguna manera' (incertidumbre). El sentido de súplica es más común, especialmente con imperativos o volitivos. Más sentido que ください. El 心よ どうか遠く空を駆けて ('corazón, por favor atraviesa el cielo') de Smile for you es una plegaria al propio corazón.
explanation.pt-BR: Expressão adverbial com dois sentidos: (1) 'por favor' (em súplica / oração) — どうか叶えて ('por favor faça realizar'); (2) 'algumamente' (em incerteza). O sentido de súplica é mais comum, especialmente com imperativos ou volitivos. Mais sentido que ください. O 心よ どうか遠く空を駆けて ('coração, por favor atravesse o céu') do Smile for you é uma prece ao próprio coração.

name: も particle (also/too, even)

explanation.en:
How it works: The particle も (mo) replaces は or が to mean 'also' or 'too'. When used with 今日 (kyou, 'today'), it implies 'today as well' — suggesting this is a repeated pleasant occurrence.

Example from this song:
• お日さまも笑ってる (ohisama mo waratteru) = 'even the sun is smiling' — も adds the sun to the list of those smiling, after みんな (everyone)
• 今日もいい天気 (kyou mo ii tenki) = 'today is also nice weather' — implies yesterday was nice too, and so is today

More examples:
• 私も行きます (watashi mo ikimasu, 'I'll go too')
• 猫も犬も好きです (neko mo inu mo suki desu, 'I like both cats and dogs')
• 明日も頑張ろう (ashita mo ganbarou, 'let's do our best tomorrow too')

Note: も replaces は and が, but stacks with other particles: にも, でも, からも.
explanation.es:
Cómo funciona: La partícula も (mo) reemplaza は o が para significar 'también'. Cuando se usa con 今日 (kyou, 'hoy'), implica 'hoy también' — sugiriendo que es una ocurrencia agradable repetida.

Ejemplo de la canción:
• お日さまも笑ってる = 'hasta el sol está sonriendo' — も agrega el sol a la lista de los que sonríen
• 今日もいい天気 = 'hoy también hace buen tiempo' — implica que ayer también hacía buen tiempo
explanation.pt-BR:
Como funciona: A partícula も (mo) substitui は ou が para significar 'também'. Quando usada com 今日 (kyou, 'hoje'), implica 'hoje também' — sugerindo que é uma ocorrência agradável repetida.

Exemplo da música:
• お日さまも笑ってる = 'até o sol está sorrindo' — も adiciona o sol à lista dos que sorriem
• 今日もいい天気 = 'hoje também está bom tempo' — implica que ontem também estava bom

name: 何も〜ない (nani mo ... nai) — nothing / not anything

explanation.en:
How it works:
The pattern 何も (nani mo) + negative verb means "nothing" or "not anything." This is part of a broader pattern where question words + も (mo) + negative = total negation: 誰も〜ない (dare mo ... nai, "nobody"), どこも〜ない (doko mo ... nai, "nowhere"), いつも〜ない (itsu mo ... nai, "never"). This is one of the first patterns beginners learn.

Example from this song:
何もない (nani mo nai) — "there is nothing"
A stark declaration of emptiness.

More examples:
• 何も食べていない (nani mo tabete inai) — "I haven't eaten anything"
• 何も心配しないで (nani mo shinpai shinaide) — "don't worry about anything"
• 誰も来なかった (dare mo konakatta) — "nobody came"

name: 受身形 (passive)

explanation.en:
How it works: For ichidan verbs, replace る with られる. For godan verbs, change the final vowel to the あ-row and add れる. This creates the passive voice — the subject receives the action.

Example from this song: 導かれて (michibikarete) = 'being guided' — from 導く (michibiku, 'to guide') → 導かれる (michibikareru, passive) → 導かれて (michibikarete, te-form)

More examples:
• 食べる (taberu, 'to eat') → 食べられる (taberareru, 'to be eaten')
• 呼ぶ (yobu, 'to call') → 呼ばれる (yobareru, 'to be called')
• 愛する (aisuru, 'to love') → 愛される (aisareru, 'to be loved')

Note: Japanese passive can express being affected (often negatively): 雨に降られた (ame ni furareta, 'I was rained on — and it bothered me'). This 'suffering passive' doesn't exist in English.

name: 頂戴 (ちょうだい) please/give me

explanation.en:
How it works: ちょうだい (choudai) is a casual/feminine way to say 'please give me' or 'please do (for me).' It's softer and cuter than ください (kudasai).

Example from this song: The song uses ちょうだい as a soft, intimate request — 'give me' or 'please do.'

More examples:
• お水ちょうだい (omizu choudai, 'give me water, please') — from お水 (omizu, 'water')
• 見せてちょうだい (misete choudai, 'show me, please') — from 見せる (miseru, 'to show')
• もう少し待ってちょうだい (mou sukoshi matte choudai, 'please wait a bit more')

Note: ちょうだい comes from 頂戴 which originally means 'to humbly receive.' As a request form, it's casual and often used by women and children, or in intimate situations. Noun + ちょうだい = 'give me (noun).' Te-form + ちょうだい = 'please do (action).'

name: "All I ever wanted" — emphatic past desire

explanation.en:
How it works:
The pattern "All I ever wanted to do was..." is an emphatic structure that distills someone's deepest, most genuine desire into a single statement. "All" means "the only thing," "ever" spans their entire life, and "wanted" places it in the past. Together, it creates a powerful gap between pure intention and tragic outcome — "I only wanted one simple thing, and yet..."

Example from this song:
"All I ever wanted to do was do right things. I never wanted to be the king." — The singer (from Eren's perspective) emphasizes that their original desire was simple and noble, but fate twisted it into something monstrous.

More examples:
• "All I ever wanted was to be free" — simple desire, complex reality
• "All she ever wanted was to be loved" — poignant gap between wish and outcome
• "All we ever wanted was peace" — collective desire contrasted with war

name: Absolute self-attribution 〜他の誰でもない / 〜以外の誰でもない

explanation.en: Pattern: noun + 他の (or 以外の) + 誰でもない = 'no one else but X.' Used for emphatic single-attribution: identifies a specific party as the absolute and only one responsible. 私 他の誰でもない = 'me — no one but me.' Compare 私だけ ('only me' — neutral): the 他の誰でもない version forces a contrast with all alternatives. Common in dramatic confessions and accusations.
explanation.es: Patrón: sustantivo + 他の (o 以外の) + 誰でもない = 'nadie más que X'. Usado para atribución única enfática: identifica a una parte específica como la única responsable. 私 他の誰でもない = 'yo — nadie más'. Compara con 私だけ ('solo yo' — neutro): la versión 他の誰でもない fuerza contraste con todas las alternativas. Común en confesiones y acusaciones dramáticas.
explanation.pt-BR: Padrão: substantivo + 他の (ou 以外の) + 誰でもない = 'mais ninguém senão X'. Usado pra atribuição única enfática: identifica parte específica como única responsável. 私 他の誰でもない = 'eu — mais ninguém'. Compare com 私だけ ('só eu' — neutro): a versão 他の誰でもない força contraste com todas as alternativas. Comum em confissões e acusações dramáticas.

name: Adjective + さ (-ness nominalizer)

explanation.en: い-adjective stem + さ creates abstract nouns: 強い → 強さ ('strength'), 弱い → 弱さ ('weakness'), 美しい → 美しさ ('beauty'), 速い → 速さ ('speed'), 高い → 高さ ('height'). Highly productive — works on virtually all い-adjectives and most な-adjectives.
explanation.es: Raíz de adjetivo い + さ forma sustantivos abstractos: 強い → 強さ, 弱い → 弱さ, 美しい → 美しさ, 速い → 速さ, 高い → 高さ. Patrón muy productivo.
explanation.pt-BR: Raiz de adjetivo い + さ cria substantivos abstratos: 強い → 強さ, 弱い → 弱さ, 美しい → 美しさ, 速い → 速さ, 高い → 高さ. Padrão muito produtivo.

name: Adjective doubling for emphasis (深い深い, 青い青い)

explanation.en: Repeating an adjective intensifies it: 深い深い ('so very deep'), 青い青い ('a deep, vivid blue'), 長い長い ('long, long...'). Common in lyrics, fairy tales, and emotive prose. The repetition lengthens the syllabic feel and adds emotional weight rather than literal stacking.
explanation.es: Repetir el adjetivo lo intensifica: 深い深い ('muy profundo'), 青い青い ('un azul muy intenso'), 長い長い. Habitual en letras, cuentos y prosa emotiva. Aporta peso emocional, no suma literal.
explanation.pt-BR: Repetir o adjetivo intensifica: 深い深い ('muito profundo'), 青い青い ('um azul muito intenso'), 長い長い. Comum em letras, contos e prosa emotiva. Acrescenta peso emocional, não soma literal.

name: Adjective stem + がる (act as if / show as)

explanation.en: い-adjective stem + がる creates a verb meaning 'show / display X (outwardly)': 強がる ('act tough'), 痛がる ('show pain'), 嬉しがる ('show joy'), 寂しがる ('act lonely'). Used to describe how someone APPEARS, not what they actually feel. Often the appearance hides a different inner feeling.
explanation.es: Raíz de adjetivo い + がる forma verbo que significa 'mostrar / aparentar X': 強がる, 痛がる, 嬉しがる, 寂しがる. Describe cómo APARENTA estar otra persona, no lo que siente.
explanation.pt-BR: Raiz de adjetivo い + がる cria verbo que significa 'demonstrar X / fingir X': 強がる, 痛がる, 嬉しがる, 寂しがる. Para descrever como ALGUÉM aparenta, não o que sente.

name: Adjective stem + すぎる (too X)

explanation.en: い-adjective stem (drop the い) + すぎる = 'too much X': 大きすぎる ('too big'), 小さすぎる ('too small'), 高すぎる ('too expensive/tall'). For な-adjectives: な-stem directly + すぎる (静かすぎる 'too quiet'). For verbs: stem + すぎる (食べすぎる 'eat too much'). Same template across all three.
explanation.es: Raíz de adjetivo い (sin el い) + すぎる = 'demasiado X': 大きすぎる, 小さすぎる, 高すぎる. Para adjetivos な: raíz + すぎる (静かすぎる). Para verbos: raíz + すぎる (食べすぎる).
explanation.pt-BR: Raiz de adjetivo い (sem o い) + すぎる = 'X demais': 大きすぎる, 小さすぎる, 高すぎる. Para adjetivos な: raiz + すぎる (静かすぎる). Para verbos: raiz + すぎる (食べすぎる).

name: Adjective stem + そう ('looks X' — for others' visible feelings)

explanation.en: い-adjective stem + そう ('looks/seems X'): 嬉しそう ('looks happy'), 悲しそう ('looks sad'), 楽しそう ('looks fun'). Used for OTHER people's visible emotions/states — you can't directly access another's feelings, only their appearance. For YOUR own emotions, use the bare adjective: 嬉しい ('I'm happy').
explanation.es: Raíz de adjetivo い + そう ('parece X'): 嬉しそう, 悲しそう, 楽しそう. Para emociones visibles de OTRAS personas — solo accedes a su apariencia. Para los TUYOS, adjetivo a secas: 嬉しい.
explanation.pt-BR: Raiz de adjetivo い + そう ('parece X'): 嬉しそう, 悲しそう, 楽しそう. Para emoções visíveis de OUTRAS pessoas — você só vê o aparente. Para os SEUS próprios sentimentos, use o adjetivo direto: 嬉しい.

name: Adjective-stem + も + ない (negative emphasis)

explanation.en: Inserting も between an adverbial adjective and a negative makes the rejection emphatic. 寂しくはない → 寂しくもない both work; 寂しくはない is the more common form. Same trick: 食べたくもない ('I have no wish to eat'), 行きたくもない ('I have zero desire to go').
explanation.es: Insertar も entre adjetivo adverbial y negativo hace el rechazo enfático. 寂しくはない → 寂しくもない. Mismo truco: 食べたくもない, 行きたくもない.
explanation.pt-BR: Inserir も entre adjetivo adverbial e negativo torna a rejeição enfática. 寂しくはない → 寂しくもない. Mesmo truque: 食べたくもない, 行きたくもない.

name: Adjective-stem nouns (V → N): 弱さ / 痛み / 終わり

explanation.en: Two productive patterns to make nouns from adjectives: (1) i-adjective + さ (formal nominalizer): 強い → 強さ ('strength'), 弱い → 弱さ ('weakness'), 美しい → 美しさ ('beauty'). (2) Verb stem (連用形) → noun: 痛む → 痛み ('pain'), 終わる → 終わり ('end'), 願う → 願い ('wish'). Rapport stacks both kinds. The 〜さ pattern is for abstract qualities; the verb-stem pattern is for actions-as-nouns.
explanation.es: Dos patrones productivos para sustantivar adjetivos: (1) adjetivo-i + さ (nominalizador formal): 強い → 強さ ('fuerza'), 弱い → 弱さ ('debilidad'), 美しい → 美しさ ('belleza'). (2) Raíz del verbo (連用形) → sustantivo: 痛む → 痛み ('dolor'), 終わる → 終わり ('fin'), 願う → 願い ('deseo'). Rapport apila los dos tipos. El 〜さ es para cualidades abstractas; la raíz verbal es para acciones-como-sustantivos.
explanation.pt-BR: Dois padrões produtivos pra fazer substantivos a partir de adjetivos: (1) adjetivo-i + さ (nominalizador formal): 強い → 強さ ('força'), 弱い → 弱さ ('fraqueza'), 美しい → 美しさ ('beleza'). (2) Raiz do verbo (連用形) → substantivo: 痛む → 痛み ('dor'), 終わる → 終わり ('fim'), 願う → 願い ('desejo'). Rapport empilha os dois tipos. O 〜さ é pra qualidades abstratas; raiz do verbo é pra ações-como-substantivos.

name: Alternation 〜ては〜返す (cyclic action)

explanation.en: Pattern that pairs a verb with another to describe a cyclical alternation. 満ちては返す ('fills-and-returns') — for tides; 行っては来る ('go-and-come') — for travels; 沈んでは浮かぶ ('sink-and-float') — for bobbing. The 〜ては (covered in Redo) marks the recurring 'each time' aspect. Kioku no Umi's 満ちては返す波 ('the wave that fills and returns') is the song's tidal metaphor: memory rises and recedes endlessly.
explanation.es: Patrón que empareja un verbo con otro para describir alternancia cíclica. 満ちては返す ('llenar-y-volver') — para mareas; 行っては来る ('ir-y-venir') — para viajes; 沈んでは浮かぶ ('hundir-y-flotar'). El 〜ては (visto en Redo) marca el aspecto recurrente 'cada vez'. El 満ちては返す波 ('la ola que llena y vuelve') de Kioku no Umi es la metáfora marea-de-memoria: la memoria sube y retrocede sin fin.
explanation.pt-BR: Padrão que pareia um verbo com outro pra descrever alternância cíclica. 満ちては返す ('encher-e-voltar') — pra marés; 行っては来る ('ir-e-vir') — viagens; 沈んでは浮かぶ ('afundar-e-flutuar'). O 〜ては (visto em Redo) marca o aspecto recorrente 'cada vez'. O 満ちては返す波 ('a onda que enche e volta') do Kioku no Umi é a metáfora maré-de-memória: a memória sobe e recua sem fim.

name: Assertion particle 〜さ (casual masculine)

explanation.en: Sentence-final particle that softens declarations into casual confidence: 'I'm telling you / I assure you.' Less weighty than ぜ (rougher), more relaxed than よ. Glory Days uses 〜さ as both sentence-end ('いつかまた会えるさ' = 'we'll meet again, you'll see') and mid-sentence filler ('無駄なことなんてさ' = 'there wasn't a single wasted thing, y'know'). The mid-sentence さ is conversational filler, like English 'like' or 'y'know.'
explanation.es: Partícula final que suaviza declaraciones en confianza casual: 'te lo digo / puedes creer'. Menos pesada que ぜ (más áspero), más relajada que よ. Glory Days usa 〜さ al final ('いつかまた会えるさ' = 'nos volveremos a ver, ya verás') y en medio ('無駄なことなんてさ' = 'no hubo una cosa en vano, ¿sabes?'). El さ intermedio es muletilla conversacional, como 'tipo' o '¿sabes?'.
explanation.pt-BR: Partícula final que abranda declarações em confiança casual: 'tô te dizendo / pode crer'. Menos pesada que ぜ (mais bruto), mais relaxada que よ. Glory Days usa 〜さ tanto no final ('いつかまた会えるさ' = 'a gente se vê de novo, viu') quanto no meio ('無駄なことなんてさ' = 'não teve uma coisa em vão, sabe'). O さ no meio é filler conversacional, tipo 'tipo' ou 'sabe'.

name: Backhanded compliment 〜にしては (for / considering it's a)

explanation.en: Pattern: noun + にしては = 'considering it's a [noun] / for a [noun].' Sets up an expectation based on the noun, then lets the predicate exceed (or underperform) it. 子供にしては大人っぽい ('mature for a child / considering she's a child, mature'); 初心者にしては上手 ('skilled for a beginner'). Hizamazuke's 豚野郎にしては やるじゃねぇか = 'for a pig bastard — not bad,' the textbook backhanded compliment.
explanation.es: Patrón: sustantivo + にしては = 'considerando que es un/a [sustantivo] / para un/a [sustantivo]'. Establece expectativa basada en el sustantivo, luego deja al predicado superarla (o no llegar). 子供にしては大人っぽい ('madura para ser una niña'); 初心者にしては上手 ('hábil para ser principiante'). El 豚野郎にしては やるじゃねぇか de Hizamazuke = 'para un cerdo desgraciado — no está mal', cumplido velado de manual.
explanation.pt-BR: Padrão: substantivo + にしては = 'considerando que é um/a [substantivo] / pra um/a [substantivo]'. Estabelece expectativa baseada no substantivo, depois deixa o predicado superar (ou ficar abaixo). 子供にしては大人っぽい ('madura pra uma criança'); 初心者にしては上手 ('habilidoso pra um iniciante'). O 豚野郎にしては やるじゃねぇか do Hizamazuke = 'pra um porco desgraçado — nada mal', elogio enviesado de manual.

name: Bungo negative 〜ぬ (literary attributive)

explanation.en: Classical Japanese negative form preserved as a literary register marker. The verb's negative stem (the part before ない) + ぬ. 届く → 届かぬ ('doesn't reach'); 離す → 離さぬ ('won't release'). Modern equivalents: 届かない / 離さない. Songs sprinkle 〜ぬ for hymn-like or samurai-era register. Black Night Town uses 届かぬ場所 ('place that doesn't reach') and 離さぬように ('so that I don't release') — both subtly archaic.
explanation.es: Negativa del japonés clásico preservada como marca de registro literario. Raíz negativa del verbo (parte antes de ない) + ぬ. 届く → 届かぬ ('no llega'); 離す → 離さぬ ('no suelto'). Equivalentes modernos: 届かない / 離さない. Las letras usan 〜ぬ para registro himno o era-samurái. Black Night Town usa 届かぬ場所 y 離さぬように — sutilmente arcaicos.
explanation.pt-BR: Negativa do japonês clássico preservada como marca de registro literário. Raiz negativa do verbo (parte antes de ない) + ぬ. 届く → 届かぬ ('não chega'); 離す → 離さぬ ('não solto'). Equivalentes modernos: 届かない / 離さない. Letras usam 〜ぬ pra registro hímnico ou era-samurai. Black Night Town usa 届かぬ場所 e 離さぬように — sutilmente arcaicos.

name: Casual / Kansai-flavoured negative 〜ん (= 〜ない)

explanation.en: 〜ん at the end of a verb is a contracted/casual/Kansai negative ending. 敵わん 'no match', 止まらん 'doesn't stop', くたばらん 'won't die', 黙らん 'won't shut up'. Common in rap/lyrics for rapid rhythm and tough register.
explanation.es: 〜ん al final del verbo es negativo contraído/casual/de Kansai. 敵わん 'no es rival', 止まらん 'no para', くたばらん 'no muere'. Frecuente en rap/letras para ritmo rápido y tono pendenciero.
explanation.pt-BR: 〜ん no fim do verbo é negativo contraído/casual/de Kansai. 敵わん 'não dá conta', 止まらん 'não para', くたばらん 'não morre'. Comum em rap/letras para ritmo rápido e tom valentão.

name: Casual conditional 〜たって (= 〜ても)

explanation.en: Past form + って is a casual equivalent of 〜ても ('even if'): つまずいたって ('even if I trip'), 雨が降ったって ('even if it rains'), 何があったって ('no matter what happens'). Common in spoken Japanese, song lyrics, rough register.
explanation.es: Forma pasada + って es equivalente casual de 〜ても ('aunque'): つまずいたって, 雨が降ったって, 何があったって. Habitual en habla coloquial y letras.
explanation.pt-BR: Forma passada + って é equivalente casual de 〜ても ('mesmo que'): つまずいたって, 雨が降ったって, 何があったって. Comum na fala coloquial e em letras.

name: Casual conditional 〜なきゃ (= 〜なければ)

explanation.en: Casual contraction of 〜なければ ('if not'). Three uses: (1) conditional 'if not / unless' — お前がいなきゃ ('if you weren't here'); (2) implied obligation — 食べなきゃ ('I have to eat,' short for 食べなきゃならない); (3) negative pre-verb conditional — that the next clause depends on. Hagane no Kokoro uses (1): 'unless you're beside me, alone I can't do anything.' Sense (2) is even more common in everyday speech — Japanese drops the predicate when it's obvious.
explanation.es: Contracción casual de 〜なければ ('si no'). Tres usos: (1) condicional 'si no / a menos que' — お前がいなきゃ ('si no estuvieras aquí'); (2) obligación implícita — 食べなきゃ ('tengo que comer', corto de 食べなきゃならない); (3) condicional pre-verbo negativo. Hagane no Kokoro usa (1): 'a menos que estés a mi lado, solo no puedo nada'. El sentido (2) es aún más común en habla cotidiana — el japonés omite el predicado.
explanation.pt-BR: Contração casual de 〜なければ ('se não'). Três usos: (1) condicional 'se não / a menos que' — お前がいなきゃ ('se você não estivesse aqui'); (2) obrigação implícita — 食べなきゃ ('preciso comer', curto de 食べなきゃならない); (3) condicional pré-verbo negativo. Hagane no Kokoro usa (1): 'a menos que você esteja ao meu lado, sozinho não consigo nada'. Sentido (2) ainda mais comum no dia a dia — o japonês deixa o predicado implícito.

name: Casual contraction 〜え / 〜ねぇ (rough masculine)

explanation.en: Vowel collapse in casual / rough masculine speech: -ai → -ee. 凄い (sugoi 'amazing') → 凄え (sugee). 知らない (shiranai) → 知らねぇ (shiranee). 危ない (abunai) → 危ねぇ (abunee). The -ee forms signal: blue-collar / shounen anime / tough-guy register. Heard in delinquent characters, sports anime, working-class dialogue. Don't use in polite or even neutral speech — but absolutely standard in shounen battle songs.
explanation.es: Colapso vocálico en habla casual / masculina áspera: -ai → -ee. 凄い (sugoi) → 凄え (sugee). 知らない → 知らねぇ. 危ない → 危ねぇ. Las formas -ee señalan: registro obrero / shounen / tipo duro. Se oyen en personajes delincuentes, animes deportivos, habla obrera. No uses en habla cortés ni neutra — pero estándar absoluto en canciones de batalla shounen.
explanation.pt-BR: Colapso vocálico na fala casual / masculina bruta: -ai → -ee. 凄い (sugoi) → 凄え (sugee). 知らない → 知らねぇ. 危ない → 危ねぇ. As formas -ee sinalizam: registro de operário / shounen / cara durão. Ouvido em personagens delinquentes, animes esportivos, fala de trabalhador. Não use em fala educada nem neutra — mas absolutamente padrão em músicas de batalha shounen.

name: Casual contraction 〜だろう → 〜だろ → 〜ろ

explanation.en: 〜だろう ('right? / probably') casually contracts to 〜だろ in everyday speech, and even further to just 〜ろ in song lyrics: 怖くなかったろ 'wasn't scary, right?'. Drop syllables for rhythm and casual tone.
explanation.es: 〜だろう ('¿no? / probablemente') se contrae a 〜だろ en el habla diaria y aún más a 〜ろ en letras: 怖くなかったろ 'no daba miedo, ¿verdad?'. Cae sílabas por ritmo y tono casual.
explanation.pt-BR: 〜だろう ('né? / provavelmente') contrai para 〜だろ no falar diário e até para 〜ろ em letras: 怖くなかったろ 'não dava medo, né?'. Cai sílabas para ritmo e tom casual.

name: Casual contraction 〜ちゃ / 〜じゃ (= 〜ては / 〜では)

explanation.en: In casual speech, 〜ては contracts to 〜ちゃ and 〜では contracts to 〜じゃ. Common pattern: 〜ちゃう = 〜てしまう ('end up doing'). Rarer pattern: 〜ちゃいない = 〜てはいない ('haven't done / am not doing'). 諦めちゃいない = 諦めてはいない ('I haven't given up') — the は inside collapses into ちゃ. Marker of confident, blue-collar masculine register.
explanation.es: En habla casual, 〜ては se contrae a 〜ちゃ y 〜では se contrae a 〜じゃ. Patrón común: 〜ちゃう = 〜てしまう ('terminar haciendo'). Más raro: 〜ちゃいない = 〜てはいない ('no he hecho / no estoy haciendo'). 諦めちゃいない = 諦めてはいない ('no me he rendido') — el は del medio colapsa en ちゃ. Marca de registro masculino casual, confiado.
explanation.pt-BR: Na fala casual, 〜ては contrai pra 〜ちゃ e 〜では contrai pra 〜じゃ. Padrão comum: 〜ちゃう = 〜てしまう ('acabar fazendo'). Mais raro: 〜ちゃいない = 〜てはいない ('não tenho/estou fazendo'). 諦めちゃいない = 諦めてはいない ('não desisti') — o は do meio colapsa em ちゃ. Marca de registro masculino casual, confiante.

name: Casual contraction 〜ちゃえば (= 〜てしまえば)

explanation.en: 〜てしまう → 〜ちゃう ('end up doing'); conditional 〜てしまえば → 〜ちゃえば ('if you just go ahead and do X'). 目をつぶっちゃえば ('if you just close your eyes'). The contraction adds a 'just go for it' feeling.
explanation.es: 〜てしまう → 〜ちゃう; condicional 〜てしまえば → 〜ちゃえば ('si vas y haces X de una'). 目をつぶっちゃえば. La contracción añade tono de 'hazlo y ya'.
explanation.pt-BR: 〜てしまう → 〜ちゃう; condicional 〜てしまえば → 〜ちゃえば ('se você simplesmente fizer X'). 目をつぶっちゃえば. A contração dá tom de 'vai logo fazer'.

name: Casual contraction 〜てった (= 〜ていった)

explanation.en: Spoken Japanese contracts 〜ていった ('went on doing') to 〜てった (or 〜とった in some regions): 上げてった = 上げていった ('kept raising'), 走ってった = 走っていった ('ran off'), 行ってった ('went away'). Same logic as 〜てた (= 〜ていた): syllable elision in the い.
explanation.es: El japonés hablado contrae 〜ていった ('fue haciendo') a 〜てった: 上げてった = 上げていった, 走ってった, 行ってった. Misma lógica que 〜てた (= 〜ていた).
explanation.pt-BR: O japonês falado contrai 〜ていった ('foi fazendo') para 〜てった: 上げてった = 上げていった, 走ってった, 行ってった. Mesma lógica de 〜てた (= 〜ていた).

name: Casual contraction 〜てても (= 〜ていても)

explanation.en: Casual collapse of 〜ていても ('even while V-ing / even if V-ed'). Drops the い from 〜いて. Used in casual speech to compress: 離れていても → 離れてても ('even if separated'), 知っていても → 知ってても ('even if knowing'). Zetsu Zetsu uses 離れてても for 'even if separated by light-years' — the casual contraction matches the song's emotional intimacy. Don't use in formal writing.
explanation.es: Colapso casual de 〜ていても ('aun mientras V / aunque V-ado'). Se cae la い de 〜いて. Se usa en habla casual para comprimir: 離れていても → 離れてても ('aunque separados'), 知っていても → 知ってても ('aunque sepa'). Zetsu Zetsu usa 離れてても para 'aunque separados por años-luz' — la contracción casual combina con la intimidad emocional. No usar en escritura formal.
explanation.pt-BR: Colapso casual de 〜ていても ('mesmo enquanto V / mesmo se V'). Cai o い de 〜いて. Usado na fala casual pra comprimir: 離れていても → 離れてても ('mesmo separados'), 知っていても → 知ってても ('mesmo sabendo'). Zetsu Zetsu usa 離れてても pra 'mesmo separados por anos-luz' — a contração casual combina com a intimidade emocional da música. Não use em escrita formal.

name: Casual contraction 〜てる (= 〜ている)

explanation.en: Spoken Japanese routinely drops the い in 〜ている → 〜てる: 感じてる = 感じている ('feeling'), やってる = やっている ('doing'), 見てる = 見ている ('watching'). Use the long form in writing/formal speech, the short form in conversation.
explanation.es: El japonés hablado suele omitir la い en 〜ている → 〜てる: 感じてる = 感じている, やってる, 見てる. Forma larga al escribir, corta al hablar.
explanation.pt-BR: O japonês falado costuma omitir o い em 〜ている → 〜てる: 感じてる = 感じている, やってる, 見てる. Use a forma longa na escrita, a curta na conversa.

name: Casual contraction 〜てんだ (= 〜ているんだ)

explanation.en: Spoken Japanese drops syllables: 〜ているんだ → 〜てるんだ → 〜てんだ. 始まってんだ = 始まっているんだ ('the thing is, it has started'). Adds explanatory tone (んだ) to a progressive (〜ている). Heavily masculine in flavor.
explanation.es: El japonés hablado omite sílabas: 〜ているんだ → 〜てるんだ → 〜てんだ. 始まってんだ = 始まっているんだ ('lo que pasa es que ya empezó'). Tono explicativo (んだ) sobre un progresivo. Sabor masculino marcado.
explanation.pt-BR: O japonês falado omite sílabas: 〜ているんだ → 〜てるんだ → 〜てんだ. 始まってんだ = 始まっているんだ ('é que já começou'). Tom explicativo (んだ) num progressivo (〜ている). Forte sabor masculino.

name: Casual contractions (わかんない, やっぱ, どっか, ポッケ)

explanation.en: The song is saturated with casual spoken contractions: わかんない (= わからない), やっぱ (= やっぱり), どっか (= どこか), ポッケ (= ポケット), メトル (= メートル). These give the speaker a young, conversational voice. Learners should recognize them in speech and anime but avoid them in formal writing.
explanation.es: La canción está llena de contracciones habladas: わかんない (= わからない), やっぱ (= やっぱり), どっか (= どこか), ポッケ (= ポケット). Dan un tono joven y coloquial. Reconocerlas en habla/anime, pero evitarlas en escritura formal.
explanation.pt-BR: A música é cheia de contrações da fala cotidiana: わかんない (= わからない), やっぱ (= やっぱり), どっか (= どこか), ポッケ (= ポケット). Dão voz jovem e coloquial. Reconhecer em fala/anime, mas evitar em escrita formal.

name: Casual contractions in spoken Japanese

explanation.en: Spoken Japanese drops syllables: している → してる ('doing'), していられない → してらんない ('can't keep doing'), でしょう → でしょ ('right?'), そのとき → そんとき ('at that time'). YUI's lyrics here use these heavily — read them as the longer formal versions.
explanation.es: El japonés hablado omite sílabas: している → してる, していられない → してらんない ('no puedo seguir'), でしょう → でしょ ('¿no?'), そのとき → そんとき ('en ese momento'). YUI usa mucho esto — léelas como la forma larga.
explanation.pt-BR: O japonês falado omite sílabas: している → してる, していられない → してらんない ('não dá pra continuar'), でしょう → でしょ ('né?'), そのとき → そんとき ('nessa hora'). As letras de YUI usam muito isso — leia como a forma longa.

name: Casual contrastive 〜けど (but)

explanation.en: Casual sentence-final or mid-sentence contrast: 'but / although.' Less formal than だが or しかし, friendlier than けれど. Often left dangling at sentence end to imply 'but [unspoken consequence].' Gurenge's 'わかってるけど…' = 'I know, but…' leaves the unspoken: there are still things kindness can't protect, even though I understand. Useful for soft pushback in conversation.
explanation.es: Contraste casual al final o medio de oración: 'pero / aunque'. Menos formal que だが o しかし, más cercano que けれど. Frecuente colgando al final para implicar 'pero [consecuencia tácita]'. El 'わかってるけど…' de Gurenge = 'lo sé, pero…' deja tácito: hay cosas que la bondad no protege, aunque lo entienda. Útil para contraposición suave en conversación.
explanation.pt-BR: Contraste casual no final ou meio de frase: 'mas / embora'. Menos formal que だが ou しかし, mais íntimo que けれど. Frequente solto no final pra implicar 'mas [consequência não dita]'. O 'わかってるけど…' do Gurenge = 'eu sei, mas…' deixa não dito: há coisas que a gentileza não protege, mesmo eu entendendo. Útil pra contraposição suave em conversa.

name: Casual emphatic 〜くって / 〜って (= 〜くて / 〜て)

explanation.en: Casual speech doubles the consonant in te-form for emphasis: 立ちたくて → 立ちたくって ('really wanting to stand'); なりたくて → なりたくって. Adds a slightly exaggerated, emotional feel — common in shouted lyrics and rough speech.
explanation.es: El habla casual duplica la consonante de la forma -te para enfatizar: 立ちたくて → 立ちたくって; なりたくて → なりたくって. Aporta un matiz exagerado, frecuente en letras gritadas y habla brusca.
explanation.pt-BR: A fala casual duplica a consoante na forma -te para dar ênfase: 立ちたくて → 立ちたくって; なりたくて → なりたくって. Acrescenta tom levemente exagerado, comum em letras gritadas e fala rude.

name: Casual quotative-ending って (= I said)

explanation.en: Sentence-final って is a casual quotative — like '(I'm telling you) X'. わかってるって ('I get it, I said'), 違うって ('I'm telling you, it's not'). Often defensive or insistent, depending on intonation.
explanation.es: って al final de frase es un quotativo casual — '(te digo que) X'. わかってるって, 違うって. Tono defensivo o insistente.
explanation.pt-BR: って no fim de frase é um quotativo casual — '(eu já disse) X'. わかってるって, 違うって. Tom defensivo ou insistente.

name: Casual reasoning 〜もん (because — colloquial)

explanation.en: Sentence-final particle from もの ('thing'). Used in casual speech to give an emotional reason / excuse: 'because (it is the way it is).' Slightly childish or feminine register, but heard widely in shounen and pop. Chozetsu Dynamic's 'ないもん' = 'because there isn't.' Compare 〜から (more neutral 'because') and 〜ので (more formal). The 〜もん softens declarations into 'this is just how it is, you see.'
explanation.es: Partícula final que viene de もの ('cosa'). En habla casual da razón / excusa emocional: 'porque (así son las cosas)'. Registro un poco infantil o femenino, pero se oye en shounen y pop. El 'ないもん' de Chozetsu Dynamic = 'porque no hay'. Compara con 〜から (más neutro 'porque') y 〜ので (más formal). El 〜もん suaviza declaraciones a 'así son las cosas, ¿sabes?'.
explanation.pt-BR: Partícula final vinda de もの ('coisa'). Na fala casual dá razão / desculpa emocional: 'porque (é assim mesmo)'. Registro um pouco infantil ou feminino, mas ouvido em shounen e pop. O 'ないもん' do Chozetsu Dynamic = 'porque não tem'. Compare com 〜から (mais neutro 'porque') e 〜ので (mais formal). O 〜もん abranda declarações em 'é só assim, sabe'.

name: Casual 〜ばっか (= 〜ばかり, only / nothing but)

explanation.en: Casual contraction of ばかり ('only / nothing but'). When attached to a verb-dictionary form + の, it modifies a noun: 通り過ぎるばっかの毎日 ('days that do nothing but pass by'). When attached to a verb te-form, it accuses the verb of being chronic: 食べてばっか ('always eating'). Heard everywhere in casual speech, almost never in writing — the kind of register shift BUMP delights in.
explanation.es: Contracción casual de ばかり ('solo / nada más que'). Con la forma de diccionario del verbo + の, modifica sustantivo: 通り過ぎるばっかの毎日 ('días que solo pasan de largo'). Con la te-forma, acusa de hábito crónico: 食べてばっか ('siempre comiendo'). Omnipresente en habla casual, casi nunca por escrito — el registro que BUMP disfruta.
explanation.pt-BR: Contração casual de ばかり ('só / nada além de'). Quando se liga à forma de dicionário do verbo + の, modifica substantivo: 通り過ぎるばっかの毎日 ('dias que só passam direto'). Com a forma-te do verbo, acusa de hábito crônico: 食べてばっか ('só fica comendo'). Onipresente na fala casual, quase nunca em texto — registro que o BUMP adora.

name: Casual ら抜き / 〜らんない (rough male contraction)

explanation.en: Two contractions of the negative potential 〜られない: 信じれる ('can believe') drops the ら (the 'standard ら抜き form'); 生きらんない ('can't live') compresses 生きられない further into 〜らんない. やってらんない ('can't keep doing this') is the most famous example. All very casual, very masculine.
explanation.es: Dos contracciones del potencial negativo 〜られない: 信じれる ('poder creer') elimina la ら ('forma ら抜き'); 生きらんない ('no poder vivir') comprime aún más 生きられない en 〜らんない. やってらんない es el caso más conocido.
explanation.pt-BR: Duas contrações do potencial negativo 〜られない: 信じれる ('conseguir acreditar') corta o ら ('forma ら抜き'); 生きらんない ('não conseguir viver') comprime ainda mais 生きられない em 〜らんない. やってらんない é o caso mais famoso.

name: Causative + て (let / make X happen — soft request)

explanation.en: Causative form + て carries a soft imperative 'let / make X happen': 積もらせて ('let them pile up'), 響かせて ('let them resonate'), 笑わせて ('let me laugh / make me laugh'). Same form covers both meanings — context decides.
explanation.es: Forma causativa + て funciona como imperativo suave 'que / hazme X': 積もらせて, 響かせて, 笑わせて. La misma forma sirve para 'déjame' y 'hazme'.
explanation.pt-BR: Forma causativa + て carrega um imperativo suave 'deixar / fazer X acontecer': 積もらせて, 響かせて, 笑わせて. A mesma forma cobre 'me deixe' e 'me faça'.

name: Causative form 〜させる / 〜せる

explanation.en: The causative form means 'make/let X do something'. Group-1 verbs take 〜せる (錆びつく → 錆びつかせる 'make rust'), Group-2 take 〜させる. Past form is 〜せた / 〜させた. 錆びつかせた恐怖心 = 'fear that I let rust over'.
explanation.es: La forma causativa significa 'hacer/dejar que X haga algo'. Verbos del Grupo 1 toman 〜せる (錆びつく → 錆びつかせる 'hacer oxidar'), Grupo 2 toman 〜させる. Pasado: 〜せた / 〜させた. 錆びつかせた恐怖心 = 'miedo que dejé oxidarse'.
explanation.pt-BR: A forma causativa significa 'fazer/deixar X fazer algo'. Verbos do Grupo 1 levam 〜せる (錆びつく → 錆びつかせる 'fazer enferrujar'), Grupo 2 levam 〜させる. Passado é 〜せた / 〜させた. 錆びつかせた恐怖心 = 'medo que deixei enferrujar'.

name: Causative 〜せる / 〜させる (make/let X do)

explanation.en: Group-1: -u → -aseru (笑う → 笑わせる 'make laugh'). Group-2: -る → -saseru (咲く is Group-1: 咲かせる 'make bloom'). The causative + imperative (笑わせろ, さかせろ, させろ) is a forceful 'make it happen!' command.
explanation.es: Grupo 1: -u → -aseru (笑う → 笑わせる 'hacer reír'). Grupo 2: -る → -saseru. Causativo + imperativo (笑わせろ, させろ) es una orden enérgica '¡hazlo pasar!'.
explanation.pt-BR: Grupo 1: -u → -aseru (笑う → 笑わせる 'fazer rir'). Grupo 2: -る → -saseru. Causativo + imperativo (笑わせろ, させろ) é um comando forte 'faça acontecer!'.

name: Causative 曇らせる (make X cloudy)

explanation.en: 曇る ('to cloud over', intransitive) → 曇らせる (causative, 'make cloudy / cloud something over'). The line uses the causative because the speaker's sigh is what's clouding the heart's lens. Productive: 喜ばせる ('make happy'), 困らせる ('cause trouble for')
explanation.es: 曇る ('nublarse', intransitivo) → 曇らせる (causativo, 'empañar algo'). La línea usa el causativo porque el suspiro empaña la lente. Productivo: 喜ばせる, 困らせる.
explanation.pt-BR: 曇る ('ficar nublado', intransitivo) → 曇らせる (causativo, 'turvar algo'). A linha usa o causativo porque o suspiro turva a lente. Produtivo: 喜ばせる, 困らせる.

name: Cinematic stacking of te-forms

explanation.en: Stacking te-forms with no other connector creates a sequence of states or actions: 無くして 気づいて 叫んで もがいて ('losing, noticing, screaming, struggling'). Each te-form leads to the next without explicit 'then'. Common in lyrics for cinematic, beat-by-beat scenes.
explanation.es: Apilar formas -te sin otro conector crea una secuencia: 無くして 気づいて 叫んで もがいて. Cada -te lleva a la siguiente sin un 'luego' explícito. En letras, da un efecto cinematográfico.
explanation.pt-BR: Empilhar formas -te sem outro conector cria sequência: 無くして 気づいて 叫んで もがいて. Cada -te leva à próxima sem 'então' explícito. Em letras, dá efeito cinematográfico.

name: Classical negative 〜ぬ (= ない)

explanation.en: An archaic equivalent of 〜ない still found in poetry, song lyrics, and set phrases. Attaches to verb a-stem: 途絶える → 途絶えぬ ('doesn't fade'); ならぬ ('won't do'). Gives the line a weighty, classical feel.
explanation.es: Equivalente arcaico de 〜ない en poesía, letras y frases hechas. Se adjunta a la raíz -a: 途絶える → 途絶えぬ ('no cesa'); ならぬ ('no puede ser'). Da peso clásico al verso.
explanation.pt-BR: Equivalente arcaico de 〜ない em poesia, letras e expressões fixas. Anexa-se ao radical -a: 途絶える → 途絶えぬ ('não cessa'); ならぬ ('não pode'). Dá peso clássico à frase.

name: Classical negative 〜ぬ / 〜ず

explanation.en: Bungo-style negative ending: 〜ぬ (attributive, before nouns) and 〜ず (adverbial, mid-sentence). The modern equivalents are 〜ない and 〜ずに / 〜ないで. Used in lyrics for solemnity. The verb 失くす becomes 失くさぬ (= 失くさない) and 抗う becomes 抗えもせず (= 抗いもしないで). 〜ず is often paired with stem forms, never with the dictionary form.
explanation.es: Final negativo estilo bungo: 〜ぬ (atributivo, antes de sustantivos) y 〜ず (adverbial, intermedio). Equivalentes modernos: 〜ない y 〜ずに / 〜ないで. En letras para dar solemnidad. 失くす se vuelve 失くさぬ (= 失くさない); 抗う se vuelve 抗えもせず (= 抗いもしないで). 〜ず se une a la raíz, nunca a la forma de diccionario.
explanation.pt-BR: Final negativo estilo bungo: 〜ぬ (atributivo, antes de substantivos) e 〜ず (adverbial, no meio da frase). Equivalentes modernos: 〜ない e 〜ずに / 〜ないで. Usado em letras para solenidade. 失くす vira 失くさぬ (= 失くさない); 抗う vira 抗えもせず (= 抗いもしないで). 〜ず se liga à raiz, nunca à forma de dicionário.

name: Classical 〜し (literary past)

explanation.en: Bungo (classical Japanese) past attributive ending — modern equivalent is 〜た. Used to give a verse the gravity of an old chronicle. 討ち取りし勇者 (literally 'the hero who slew') would be 討ち取った勇者 in modern Japanese. Modern songs sprinkle it for archaic flavor; using it everywhere would sound stilted, but a single 〜し in an opening verse signals 'this is myth-time.'
explanation.es: Final atributivo de pasado del japonés clásico (bungo) — equivalente moderno es 〜た. Se usa para dar peso de crónica antigua. 討ち取りし勇者 ('el héroe que abatió') sería 討ち取った勇者 hoy. Las canciones modernas lo usan en pequeñas dosis para sabor arcaico; usarlo todo el tiempo sonaría forzado, pero un solo 〜し en el verso inicial señala 'esto es tiempo mítico'.
explanation.pt-BR: Final atributivo de passado do japonês clássico (bungo) — equivalente moderno é 〜た. Usado para dar peso de crônica antiga. 討ち取りし勇者 ('o herói que abateu') seria 討ち取った勇者 hoje. Músicas modernas usam um pouquinho para sabor arcaico; usar sempre soaria forçado, mas um único 〜し no verso inicial sinaliza 'isto é tempo de mito'.

name: Classical/literary endings: 〜き〜かな

explanation.en: い-adjective + き (instead of い) is the classical attributive form, and かな is a literary exclamation (≈ '...alas!' / 'how X!'). 遣る瀬無きかな ≈ 'how disconsolate it is, alas'. Reserved for poetry, song lyrics, and formal writing for emotional weight.
explanation.es: Adjetivo い + き (en lugar de い) es la forma atributiva clásica, y かな es exclamación literaria (≈ '¡ay, qué...!'). 遣る瀬無きかな ≈ '¡qué melancolía tan inconsolable!'. Reservado a poesía, letras y escritura formal.
explanation.pt-BR: Adjetivo い + き (em vez de い) é a forma atributiva clássica, e かな é exclamação literária (≈ 'ai... que'). 遣る瀬無きかな ≈ 'que melancolia inconsolável!'. Reservado para poesia, letras e escrita formal.

name: Classical/literary negative 〜ぬ (= 〜ない)

explanation.en: An archaic negative ending found in poetry, song lyrics, and set phrases. Attaches to verb a-stem: 鳴り止む → 鳴り止まぬ ('doesn't stop ringing'). Lends weight and timeless feel.
explanation.es: Terminación negativa arcaica en poesía, letras y frases hechas. Se adjunta a la raíz -a: 鳴り止む → 鳴り止まぬ ('no deja de sonar'). Aporta peso y atemporalidad.
explanation.pt-BR: Terminação negativa arcaica em poesia, letras e expressões fixas. Anexa-se ao radical -a: 鳴り止む → 鳴り止まぬ ('não para de soar'). Dá peso e atemporalidade.

name: Cleft sentence: 〜のは〜から / 〜のは〜だ

explanation.en: Focus structure that promotes a clause to subject and explains its WHY in the predicate. Pattern: '[clause]のは[reason]から' = 'the (fact / time / reason) that [clause] is because [reason].' Glory Days uses it to deliver the chorus thesis: '走れたのは 君がそばにいたから' ('the reason I could run was because you were beside me'). Compare neutral '君がそばにいたから走れた' ('I could run because you were beside me'): the cleft adds emphasis to the WHY.
explanation.es: Estructura de foco que promueve una cláusula a sujeto y explica el PORQUÉ en el predicado. Patrón: '[cláusula]のは[razón]から' = 'el (hecho / tiempo / motivo) de [cláusula] es porque [razón]'. Glory Days la usa para entregar la tesis del estribillo: '走れたのは 君がそばにいたから' ('la razón de que pudiera correr fue porque estabas a mi lado'). Compara neutro '君がそばにいたから走れた': la escindida añade énfasis al PORQUÉ.
explanation.pt-BR: Estrutura de foco que promove uma cláusula a sujeito e explica o PORQUÊ no predicado. Padrão: '[cláusula]のは[razão]から' = 'o (fato / tempo / motivo) de [cláusula] é porque [razão]'. Glory Days usa para entregar a tese do refrão: '走れたのは 君がそばにいたから' ('o motivo de eu poder correr foi porque você estava ao meu lado'). Compare neutro '君がそばにいたから走れた': a clivada acrescenta ênfase ao PORQUÊ.
